newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks close up, boosted by foreign buyers.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks close up, boosted by foreign buyers.

text.p: Shares prices in Madrid closed higher on Tuesday in moderate volume, amid bond gains and buying by foreign investors, dealers said.

The bourse got a shot in the arm from news the government is considering a cut in spending in real terms in 1997, rather than a freeze as originally indicated. News that the budget is likely to get parliamentary support helped too, dealers said.
But they added that the tone may be cautious until specific details emerge.
The general index rose 2.50 points, 0.70 percent, to 357.81 and the Ibex added 34.54 points, 0.85 percent, to 4,075.53.
Energy group Repsol added 60 pesetas to 4,100, recovering part of a long run of losses ahead of results, due this week.

Telefonica continued to climb helped by buy recommendations from foreign brokers, based on strong growth expectations for the firm, dealers said. The stock closed up 25 pesetas at 2,390 with about 4.5 million shares traded.
Volume today recovered well, with around 29 billion shares changing hands.
